findings.how_to_check: Review CODE/compute_subgroup_linkage_rates.do to verify that no bias metric, selection model, or balance test between linked and population samples is computed, and compare line 797 with line 784 of DHTS-2026-10-12.tex.
findings.suggested_fix: Revise line 797 of DHTS-2026-10-12.tex to claim only improved transcription quality and expanded sample coverage across subgroups, deleting the unproven assertion of reduced demographic and geographic biases.
findings.title: Conclusion claims reduced demographic and geographic bias without empirical estimation or support
findings.what_the_code_does: For each demographic subgroup, the code computes only baseline and post-improvement linkage rates ('summarize linked_before' and 'summarize linked_after') and their percentage difference. It does not estimate selection into the link, assess downstream estimand bias, or evaluate geographic representativeness. While line 784 explicitly acknowledges that whether linking gains translate into less biased estimates is an unsettled question requiring resemblance between newly linked and unlinked records, line 797 directly asserts that the method 'reduces demographic and geographic biases.'
findings.why_it_matters: Proportional increases in linkage rates across subgroups do not imply reduced selection bias or more representative samples; under-linked groups may remain substantially under-represented. Asserting bias reduction in the final conclusion over-claims what the empirical design demonstrates and directly contradicts the paper's own caveat at line 784.

findings.how_to_check: Run 'git grep non_english' across CODE and replication to confirm that non_english_mtongue is used only for linkage rates in compute_subgroup_linkage_rates.do, never for transcription disagreement rates.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add mother-tongue disagreement computation to make_balance_exhibits.do and verify it, or split the claim into separate foreign-born (MATCH) and non-English (UNCHECKED/NOCODE) entries in replication/claims.toml.
findings.title: Claim checker marks abstract non-English disagreement claim as MATCH despite having no producing code or test
findings.what_the_code_does: The registered claim 'abstract-disagree-groups' covers the draft text 'with higher disagreement rates for foreign-born individuals and non-English speakers', but its assert expression checks only foreign-born rates in figures/incongruent_allstates.tex. As acknowledged in the registry issue, non_english_mtongue is not in the balance table and no script computes disagreement for non-English speakers. Yet check_claims.py marks the claim MATCH, and HANDOFF.md and replication/README.md report 48 match and 0 fail.
findings.why_it_matters: A substantive empirical claim in the abstract regarding non-English speakers is unverified, while the replication pipeline and handoff docs report a false clean bill of health with zero failing claims.

findings.how_to_check: Inspect replication/results/compute_legibility_quartiles.tex to confirm Q2 and Q3 are omitted, and run 'table leg_q, contents(mean linked_before mean linked_after)' in Stata to inspect gains across all four quartiles.
findings.suggested_fix: Export percentage gains for all four quartiles in CODE/compute_legibility_quartiles.do and assert 'legGainLowest > legGainQ2 and legGainLowest > legGainQ3 and legGainLowest > legGainHighest'. Alternatively, soften line 783 to state that gains are substantially higher in the lowest than highest legibility quartile.
findings.title: Claim that gains are greatest where records are hardest to read is asserted without checking middle quartiles
findings.what_the_code_does: CODE/compute_legibility_quartiles.do partitions records into four quartiles using 'xtile leg_q = legibility, nq(4)', but exports linkage gains only for Q1 ('legGainLowest') and Q4 ('legGainHighest'). In replication/claims.toml, 'conclusion-hardest-to-read' asserts 'legGainLowest > legGainHighest and legGainLowest > linkGainAll'. The registry note acknowledges that quartiles 2 and 3 are not in the results file. This test does not prove that Q1 has the largest gain across the distribution.
findings.why_it_matters: The conclusion claims gains are largest ('by most') where records are hardest to read, but the code does not verify whether Q2 or Q3 gains exceed Q1. Replacing a previously contradicted subgroup claim with another unverified superlative risks referee challenge.

findings.how_to_check: Inspect replication/run_machineA.do and replication/README.md under 'What is not covered' to verify that ML pipeline execution and Table 1 generation scripts are absent.
findings.suggested_fix: Provide code, environment specifications, and evaluation entry points for the ML pipeline, or archive model weights, sample inference scripts, and the evaluation script computing Table 1 from model predictions.
findings.title: Replication package omits ML training, inference, and character-accuracy evaluation code for Table 1
findings.what_the_code_does: The replication archive is strictly an analysis-tier pipeline operating on pre-built frozen intermediate files (43 GB labeled data, 49 state merged files, and temp.dta). As documented in replication/README.md, no code is provided for image preprocessing, line segmentation, character extraction, model training, prediction, or ditto resolution, and Table 1's reported accuracy figures (97.38%, 98.61%, 94.54%, 98.29%) are hand-typed with no producing script.
findings.why_it_matters: An independent replicator cannot verify or reproduce the machine learning model's reported transcription accuracy or re-generate transcriptions from census records, leaving the core methodological contribution of the paper unverifiable from the archive.

review_limits: External intermediate datasets (e.g., 43 GB census1940_all_labeled_data.dta, 22 GB temp.dta, and 50 merged_<state>1940.dta files on external drives) could not be loaded into memory or inspected directly.
The full Stata replication pipeline was not executed; runtime behavior and empirical values were inferred from code logic, exported LaTeX tables, and saved .tex result macros.
The machine learning pipeline (segmentation, model weights, character extraction, CRNN/Transformer inference) is external and was not available for inspection.
The review was conducted in a read-only inspection mode; no code modifications or diagnostic scripts were run against raw census data.
summary: The unified 51,036,859 analysis sample resolves the earlier sample-gap hazard, and draft counts and rates now match the committed results. However, the claim checker's '48 match / 0 fail' headline masks that the abstract's non-English disagreement claim is completely untested, the conclusion's superlative legibility gain is not verified against middle quartiles, and the draft still claims reduced demographic and geographic bias without estimation. The single most important fix before submission is to align the conclusion's bias-reduction claim with the paper's actual empirical design.
